csap_ctrl_global_offset_table_got_and_po.code:
.global my_pic_func
.type my_pic_func, @function

my_pic_func:
# Access external symbol 'target_var' via GOT/PIC

# 1. Calculate address of target_var's entry in the GOT
#    (Using PC-relative addressing: RIP + offset)
    movq    target_var@GOTPCREL(%rip), %rax

# 2. Load the absolute address (resolved by dynamic loader)
#    from the Global Offset Table entry pointed to by RAX
    movq    (%rax), %rbx

# 3. Access the data using the resolved absolute address
    movl    (%rbx), %ecx

    ret
.size my_pic_func, .-my_pic_func

.section .text
.global my_func
my_func:
    ; Standard Prologue (Analysis Focus)
    push rbp         ; Save old Frame Pointer
    mov rbp, rsp     ; Set new Frame Pointer

    ; Data Movement & Arithmetic
    ; RDI = Arg1, RSI = Arg2
    mov rax, rdi     ; rax = Arg1 (Return register)
    sub rax, rsi     ; rax = Arg1 - Arg2
    mov rcx, 0xA     ; Constant
    cmp rax, rcx     ; Compare (sets FLAGS)
    jl .L_Less_Than  ; Conditional jump

.L_Continue:
    ; Epilogue
    mov rsp, rbp     ; Deallocate stack frame
    pop rbp          ; Restore old frame
    ret

.L_Less_Than:
    add rax, 1       ; rax++
    jmp .L_Continue

csap_proc_processor_pipelining_and_hazar.code:
; Pipelining: Data Hazard (RAW) Mitigation
; Load/Use dependencies cause stalls (5-cycle latency common)

; --- Stalled Sequence Example ---
mov r10, [rdi]    ; Load R10 (Latency begins)
inc r10           ; RAW Hazard: Pipeline stalls
mov [rsi], r10    ; Store

; --- Instruction Scheduled (Optimized) ---
mov r10, [rdi]    ; Load R10
mov r11, [r8]     ; Independent instruction 1 (Fills delay slot)
add r11, 42       ; Independent instruction 2
inc r10           ; R10 ready; Stall avoided
mov [rsi], r10    ; Store result

; Avoid long dependency chains for better throughput.

csap_sys_machine_level_programming_with_.code:
; Basic Data Movement and Arithmetic
movq $10, %rax
movq $20, %rbx
addq %rbx, %rax    ; RAX = 30
subq $5, %rax      ; RAX = 25
imulq %rbx, %rax   ; RAX = 500 (RAX = RAX * RBX)
cqto               ; Sign-extends RAX (64-bit) into RDX:RAX (128-bit)
idivq %rcx         ; RDX:RAX / RCX -> RAX=quotient, RDX=remainder

; Memory Addressing Modes (RDI = base address)
movq $0xDEADBEEF, %rax
movq %rax, (%rdi)       ; Store RAX at address RDI
movq $42, 8(%rdi)       ; Store 42 at RDI + 8
movq (%rdi, %rsi, 4), %rbx ; Load RBX = mem[RDI + RSI*4]

; Linux Syscall: write(fd=1, buf=RSI, count=RDX)
movq $1, %rax     ; Syscall number for write
movq $1, %rdi     ; Argument 1: File descriptor (stdout)
movq %rbx, %rsi   ; Argument 2: Buffer pointer
movq $14, %rdx    ; Argument 3: Length
syscall           ; Execute kernel request (Return value in RAX)

; Function Entry/Exit (ABI)
_func_name:
    pushq %rbp
    movq %rsp, %rbp
    ; ... body using args RDI, RSI, RDX
    movq $0, %rax     ; Return value
    popq %rbp
    ret

exp_op_linker_symbol_resolution_order_an.topic: Linker Symbol Resolution Order and Its Impact on Static Linking
exp_op_linker_symbol_resolution_order_an.code:
# Linker Symbol Resolution Order (Static Link Libraries)
# Order matters: Libraries must appear AFTER objects/libraries
# that reference the symbols they define. (Left-to-Right processing)

# Scenario: main.o needs B, B needs A

# CORRECT ORDER: B defined before A is satisfied
gcc main.o -lB -lA -o program

# INCORRECT ORDER: A is defined, but later B requires A.
# Linker 'forgets' unused symbols from A when processing main/B.
gcc main.o -lA -lB -o program
# (Result: Unresolved reference to func_A)

# Handling Circular Dependencies (Mutual Needs): Use Grouping
gcc main.o -Wl,--start-group -lA -lB -Wl,--end-group -o program
# (Forces repeated search through all libraries in the group)
